the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Apply the local-source lemma with g = id, Q = locally of finite presentation, R = flat and locally of finite presentation, P = Cohen-Macaulay, via the local-source-apply remark: this gives an open U' of U with t^{-1}(U') the largest open subscheme of R on which s is Cohen-Macaulay, proving (1). Let i be the inverse of the groupoid; since i is an isomorphism with s composed with i = t and t composed with i = s, the open s^{-1}(U') is likewise the largest open on which t is Cohen-Macaulay, proving (2). By the flat-finite-presentation-CM-open lemma the CM-locus open is dense in every fibre of the flat finitely presented structure map; since the structure maps have the identity section, density in every fibre gives nonempty intersection, i.e. surjectivity, proving (3) and symmetrically (4). Part (5) is a formal consequence of (1), (2) and the restriction discussion of the groupoids chapter: on R' = s^{-1}(U') intersect t^{-1}(U') the restriction (U', R', s', t', c') is a groupoid whose source and target are Cohen-Macaulay (each lies in the respective largest CM-open) and locally of finite presentation (restrictions of locally finite presentation morphisms). (source lines 862-887)
